first.rationale: Verify the two most consequential and competing beliefs: onboarding simplification directly addresses the current completion and activation declines, while promotional pricing responds to competitive pressure but may create lower-quality or less sustainable revenue. I currently favor a standard, guarded onboarding experiment because it can improve activation and time-to-value without sacrificing monetization or attracting poor-fit accounts; completion gains should not be assumed to equal qualified revenue gains.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, because the verified result shows higher completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and improved 30-day retention—directly addressing both current completion and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing: although it drove short-term qualified-revenue lift, the 12% retention decline indicates poor renewal durability. Evaluate onboarding with qualified revenue, activation, time-to-value, and retention guardrails rather than completion alone.
